title: La pila
desc: Water comes twice a week and you have to catch it
setting: Roberto finds you standing in the yard with an empty bucket and no idea what to do.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Chele, el agua viene hoy. ¿Ya llenaste la pila?
steps.en: Chele, the water comes today. Have you filled the tank?

options.en: Not yet. What time does it come?
options.feedback: Admits you have not, and asks the one thing you need to know. Nothing wasted.
Fair question on day one, but you have one in your own yard and he can see it.

options.es: Yo tengo agua en la llave.
options.en: I have water in the tap.
options.feedback: That is the point - today you do, tomorrow you will not.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Como a las seis. Después se va y no vuelve hasta el jueves.
steps.en: About six. Then it goes and does not come back until Thursday.

options.es: Entonces lleno todo lo que pueda.
options.en: Then I will fill everything I can.
options.feedback: Exactly the right instinct, and said in one clean sentence.
You have understood but not acted. Here the answer is what you are going to do.
True, and there is nothing to be done about it. Fill the tank.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Agarrá el balde. Yo te ayudo.
steps.en: Grab the bucket. I will help you.

options.feedback: Dale pues accepts the offer the way a neighbour would.

options.en: No, I can do it alone.
options.feedback: You can, but turning down help from a neighbour here is turning down more than help.

options.en: How much will you charge me?
options.feedback: He is not selling you anything. That question would sting.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Listo. Con esto aguantás hasta el jueves.
steps.en: Done. This will see you through to Thursday.

options.feedback: Perfect. The debt is the point, and vos is exactly right with him.
Correct and warm, just a shade formal for a chavalo you see every day.

options.en: I do not need anything else now.
options.feedback: It closes the door on him. He was not asking whether you needed more.
